h1: The 6 Best Lightweight Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six lightweight lawn mowers from reel to cordless, sorted by cutting width, power source and the yard each one suits.
summary: The EGO POWER+ 21 inch is the best lightweight lawn mower for a standard lawn: a full-width cordless push mower with its battery and charger. The Greenworks 40V 16 inch suits smaller lawns, and the Litheli is the cheap brushless cordless option. The reel and corded models fit small yards.
intro: Shoppers hunting for a light mower tend to compare the weight printed on the box and skip the power source, which is the thing that actually changes how the machine feels in the hand. A corded mower makes you drag a cable, a battery mower carries its cell on board, and a reel mower carries nothing but blades. The right choice depends on how much grass you have and where the outlet sits.

We reviewed six mowers on paper, covering a manual reel, corded electrics and cordless models from 12 to 21 inches. They were ranked on cutting width against manageability, power-source convenience, adjustability and the type of lawn each suits, using spec sheets and owner feedback. Most listings omit weight, so we judged lightness from design rather than from invented figures.

products.name: EGO POWER+ 21-Inch Cordless Electric Lawn Mower with Battery and Charger (LM2114)
products.verdict: A full 21-inch cut from the lightest cordless full-width mower ranked here.
products.description:
EGO's POWER+ LM2114 cuts a 21 inch swath on the 56V battery platform, pushes by hand, and ships with its battery and charger. A push drive keeps the weight down compared with self-propelled mowers, and a cordless design means no cable to drag around the trees.

It ranks first because a full-width deck and a complete kit come from a mower that stays manageable. The Greenworks is lighter to handle but narrower, and the corded models limit your range.

Buy it for a standard lawn where fewer passes matter. The caveats are storage space for the wider deck and a price above small-yard models. Skip it if your yard is a garden strip that a 14 inch mower handles easily.
products.idealFor: Standard-size lawns where you want fewer passes without a heavy self-propelled mower.
products.skipIf: Your yard is a small patio or garden strip that a 14-inch mower handles easily.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Mower with 4.0Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A sensible 16-inch cordless push mower for small to mid-size lawns.
products.description:
Greenworks packs a 4.0Ah battery and charger with this 16 inch, 40V push mower. The compact deck is easy to turn around beds and corners, and being cordless means no cable catches on shrubs.

It ranks second because the narrower deck needs more passes than the EGO, and runtime limits a larger lawn. It beats the Litheli on battery size and brand support.

Buy it for a small to mid-size lawn where you want cordless power without a heavy deck. Skip it if you mow a large lawn and want the fewest passes. Charge the battery before each mow, and expect to finish a medium lawn on one pack.
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size lawns where you want cordless power without a heavy deck.
products.skipIf: You mow a large lawn and want the fewest possible passes.

products.name: Litheli Cordless Lawn Mower 14-Inch, Brushless Motor with 5.0Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: The cheapest way into a cordless brushless mower for a small yard.
products.description:
Litheli's 14 inch cordless mower runs a brushless motor from a 5.0Ah battery that comes with a charger, offers five cutting heights and costs between $50 and $100. A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat, which stretches the runtime of a battery that size.

It ranks third because the 14 inch deck is narrow and the brand is less known. It is the cheapest way into a cordless brushless mower.

Buy it for a small yard under about 3,000 square feet on a tight budget. Skip it if you have a standard-size lawn and want a wide deck. Five height positions give you flexibility through the season.
products.idealFor: Small yards under about 3,000 square feet on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You have a standard-size lawn and want a wide deck.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K Electric Corded Lawn Mower, 15-Inch, 11 Amp
products.verdict: An 11 amp corded push mower with more width than a reel mower.
products.description:
LawnMaster's MEB1114K pairs an 11 amp motor with a 15 inch deck and a power cord, pushed by hand. With no battery to replace, it offers steady power as long as the cable reaches. It is wider than the reel mowers below.

It ranks fourth because the cord limits your range and snags on obstacles. It works best on open ground close to an outlet.

Buy it for a small, open yard near an outlet. Skip it if your lawn has trees, beds or corners that would snag a cord. Work away from the outlet in rows so you never run over the cable, and use a cord that is rated for outdoor use.
products.idealFor: Small open yards near an outlet.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has trees, beds or corners that would snag a cord.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch 4-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: No battery, no cord, no fuel: the lightest way to cut a small lawn.
products.description:
American Lawn Mower's 1204-14 is a four-blade, 14 inch reel that you push by hand, with no battery, cord or fuel to manage. A reel mower is the lightest option here because there is no motor to carry, and the blades make a clean scissor cut on short grass.

It ranks fifth because it needs regular mowing and struggles in tall grass. It beats the corded models on weight and quiet.

Buy it for a small, flat lawn that gets mowed often. Skip it if you let the grass grow tall between cuts. Low running cost is its quiet appeal, and there is almost nothing to maintain beyond blade contact.
products.skipIf: You let the grass grow tall between cuts.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 3-in-1 Corded Lawn Mower, Weed Eater, and Edger (BESTA512CM)
products.verdict: A small 12-inch corded tool that doubles as a trimmer and edger.
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's BESTA512CM is a 6.5 amp corded 12 inch tool that switches between mowing, trimming and edging. It is the smallest and easiest to store, and a single tool covers three jobs on a small plot.

It ranks last because the 12 inch deck is too small for a main mower and the cord limits range. The price is low.

Buy it for small patches and edging around a patio. Skip it if you need a main mower for a whole lawn. Treat it as a supplement, not a replacement, and keep the cord clear of the blade. The price is low, but the small deck means long sessions.
products.idealFor: Small patches and edging around a patio.
products.skipIf: You need a main mower for a whole lawn.

methodology.description: Every pick is matched to the lawn size and type its spec sheet supports.

whatMatters.detail: Cutting width is the deck size in inches, and it sets how many passes a lawn needs. A 21-inch deck covers a stripe 50 percent wider than a 14-inch one. Check the number in the product title, not a marketing phrase on the box, and compare it with the size of your lawn so you know how many extra passes a narrow deck adds.

Power source means manual reel, corded electric or battery. Corded mowers need an outlet and a cable, and battery mowers need charging. Look for the amp or volt figure in the title to tell which type you are buying. The LawnMaster lists 11 amp, the EGO 56V and the Greenworks 40V, and the reel lists nothing.

Some cordless listings sell the bare tool only. A battery and charger can cost a large share of the total. Confirm the listing says battery and charger included and note the Ah rating, since higher Ah means longer runtime. The EGO, Greenworks and Litheli here include both, which is a point in their favor.

Height adjustment sets how tall the grass stays after cutting. More positions let you adapt to season and lawn type. Look for a stated number of positions, like five, on the spec sheet. The Litheli lists five, and the others give no figure, so check the manual for the range before you buy.

Drive type is push or self-propelled. Self-propelled adds a motor and weight, while push keeps the machine light. Every pick here is push or manual, so check the listing if you want more assistance, and remember that a light mower trades some help on slopes for easier handling, which suits flat yards best.

faq.q: Is a corded or cordless mower lighter?
faq.a: The spec sheets here do not list weights, so check each listing. Corded mowers carry no battery, but you drag a cable. A reel mower carries no motor at all, so it is the lightest in practice, though you provide all the power.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with light mowers?
faq.a: They buy by weight alone and end up with a deck too narrow for their lawn. A 14-inch deck on a standard lawn means many extra passes, so match the width to the yard first, then think about weight.

faq.q: Is the EGO worth it over the Greenworks?
faq.a: If your lawn is standard size, the 21-inch deck saves real time. For a small lawn, the 16-inch Greenworks is easier to handle and stays in the same bracket.

faq.q: Does a reel mower need setup?
faq.a: The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 uses a manual 4-blade reel with no battery or fuel. Set your height, then push. Mow often so the grass stays short, because a reel stalls in tall stems.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless mower?
faq.a: Store the battery indoors, charge it with the supplied charger and clear grass from the deck after use. Check the listing for each brand's care guidance, especially for the EGO and Greenworks batteries, and keep them out of freezing garages.

faq.q: Can I use a corded mower on a large lawn?
faq.a: You can, but cable management becomes tedious. The LawnMaster is best for small, open yards near an outlet, and a long extension cord adds trip hazards and voltage loss.

finalTake: The EGO POWER+ 21 inch is the right lightweight mower for a standard lawn, since it pairs a full deck with a complete cordless kit. Choose the Greenworks 40V for smaller yards and a reel mower only for tiny, flat ones. Pick the deck width before the weight.
